heroHeadline: 223rd Flag Day Passed Amid Collapse; MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 10 Closed; GSF ~800 Personnel in First Full Week Under Gen. Batsuuri — MSF Partially Resumes Elsewhere in Port-au-Prince
heroSubtitle: Haiti marked its 223rd Flag Day on May 18, 2026, as Latin Times reported the national holiday passed 'amid deepening security crisis as gang violence continues to claim numerous lives.' MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only emergency medical facility for the commune's approximately 300,000 residents — entered its tenth consecutive day of closure on May 19, with no announced reopening timeline. MSF announced a partial resumption of medical activities at its other Port-au-Prince facilities, but the Cité Soleil site remains closed as gang conditions still prevent safe access. UN BINUH's provisional toll from the May 9–14 intra-Viv Ansanm clashes stands at 78 killed and 66 wounded (at least 10 confirmed civilians); the broader March 5–May 11 toll for Cité Soleil and Croix-des-Bouquets is 305 killed and 277 wounded, including 63 confirmed civilian residents. Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri completed his first full week commanding the GSF — approximately 800 personnel (Chad 400+, Guatemala ~75, El Salvador ~70) all concentrated in Port-au-Prince's city center, leaving Cité Soleil, the Cul-de-Sac Plain, and the entire Artibonite without international security coverage. $59M disbursed of $200M+ pledged; full 5,500-person strength expected fall–end 2026. Separately, 107 Haitian nationals deported from the Bahamas arrived on Flag Day, adding to Haiti's 1.47M+ internally displaced. PM Fils-Aimé's declaration that August 30 elections are 'impossible' stands; no electoral decree issued; 23 communes inaccessible.
